The word "and" is represented by the symbol "$\land$", while the word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor$".

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

- **Part 1:** $6|10$ and $6|18.$ This corresponds to
\[
\underbrace{6|10}_M \quad 
\underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{and}}_{\land} \quad 
\underbrace{6|18}_P
\]
that is, $M \land P.$

- **Part 2:** $11$ is prime and odd. This corresponds to
\[
\underbrace{11 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is prime}}_N \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{and}}_{\land} \quad 
\underbrace{11 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is odd }}_Q,
\]
that is, $N \land Q.$

So, we can express the sentence as
\[
\underbrace{6|10 \textbf{ and } 6|18}_{M \, \land \, P} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad 
\underbrace{11 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is prime } \textbf{and} \textrm{ odd }}_{N \, \land \, Q},
\]
that is, $(M \land P) \lor (N \land Q).$
